depth_mwe.locator: Sec. 4 and Conclusions, Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A 511 (2003) 347 (hep-ex/0306014)
depth_mwe.note: Effective vertical depth for a flat surface, found by comparing the measured muon intensity with calculation, for a measured vertical depth of 1070 m (the site record keeps the 1.1 km of the laboratory page). Pandola 2011 gives 2850 m w.e. as the minimum and 3450 m w.e. as the average overburden; Mei & Hime Table I: 2.805 ± 0.015 km.w.e.
depth_mwe.quote: This shows an effective vertical depth of 2805±45 metres of water equivalent

muon_flux.locator: Abstract and Sec. 4, Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A 511 (2003) 347 (hep-ex/0306014)
muon_flux.note: Measured with the one-tonne ZEPLIN-I liquid-scintillator veto detector, counting muons that deposit 30 MeV or more; (4.09 ± 0.08 stat. ± 0.13 syst.) in the text. The paper's vertical intensity, 3.32 × 10^-8 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1, is not a flux and is not recorded. Pandola 2011 quotes 4.1 × 10^-4 m^-2 s^-1; Mei & Hime Table I (Boulby row) and Woodley et al. 2024 Table III repeat (4.09 ± 0.15) × 10^-8 cm^-2 s^-1. The quote's factor 10^-8 multiplies the whole bracket, so the stored value is 4.09 × 10^-8 cm^-2 s^-1 with no unit conversion.
muon_flux.quote: The muon flux in the laboratory is found to be (4.09±0.15)×10−8 cm−2 s−1

name: Boulby Mine (site of the underground laboratory)

summary.plain: An underground laboratory inside a working mine on the North Yorkshire coast of England, more than a kilometre below the North York Moors.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory hosted within the ICL-UK Boulby mine (potash/polyhalite), North Yorkshire, at ~1.1 km depth beneath the North York Moors.
